top.line: A website where investors use our tools
top.para: An article brief for investor.sgit.ai: because what we build has to be experienced, investors and founders should use it, with news, contracts as graphs, deal rooms as vaults, an evaluation framework and sgit as the case study, run by agents and shown to investors.

in-short.line: Eight lines from the brief to asking investors
in-short.para: An article brief; experience explains; one site for investors and founders; eight sections; the lost evaluation framework returns; run by agents; built to the house rules with CI owning the version; then ask investors what helps.

why.line: Investors should use the technology, not read about it
why.para: Vaults, read keys, agents with keys and behaviour policies sound abstract until opened. The pieces exist on this site, the investor deck, the deal room vaults, the insurance calculator; what is missing is one place for investors and founders where they are the website.

sections.line: News, contracts, founders, models, vaults, keys, cases
sections.para: Angel and Series A news as a graph; term sheets and cap tables linked clause to clause; a founders' section; funding models from open source to proprietary; deal rooms as vaults; keys for investors; sgit as a published case study and RiskMandate at work.

framework.line: The March framework scores security startups to forty
framework.para: The GenAI cybersecurity startup evaluation framework scores seven criteria and an architecture meta-criterion from 1 to 5, with bands from Rare to Avoid. It is not yet a maturity model: no levels, and no team, traction or financials, by design.

team.line: A small scheduled agent team, fed by the newsroom's wire
team.para: Like the PHP newsroom's two people and nineteen agents, but smaller: conductor, journalist, researcher, security and observability. The news could come from a newsroom wire vault the site reads, which shows what vaults are for.

rules.line: sgit.ai's repository rules, with CI owning the version
rules.para: A brief in full, a reality file, a corrections file, a gate, real tests, a review folder, roles as files, md twins and llms.txt, read keys only. CI picks every version; the site points to coding, nfrs and ux.sgit.ai.

ask.line: Show it to investors, and record what they say
ask.para: Once a first version runs, email investors and ask whether it is useful and what would help; the answers decide the site and go on the record.

limits.line: A brief: nothing built, and a framework not a model
limits.para: None of it is built; the framework scores but has no levels; the news needs public sources and no private names; The Cyber Boardroom repository's link is to come; sgit's raise is not published.

sources.line: Two memos, a research agent, and a build brief
sources.para: From Dinis's two memos of 28 October, kept word for word; the framework, the PHP newsroom and sgit.ai's guidance read from their own pages on 29 October; the build brief for the site's agent is in the repository notes.
